answer_raw:
The newest iPhone lineup is the **iPhone Duo** [1].

## Pricing and Specs
The current flagship pricing for the new lineup is as follows:

| Model | Price (MSRP) |
| :--- | :--- |
| **iPhone Duo** (256GB) | **$1,999** (as of 2026-09-13) [5] |
| **iPhone 18 Pro** | **$1,199** (as of 2026-09-13) [5] |
| **iPhone 18 Pro Max** | **$1,299** (as of 2026-09-13) [5] |

The **iPhone 18 Pro** features a **48MP Fusion Main camera** with **variable aperture** ($f/1.48, f/1.8, f/2.8, f/4.0$), which is a significant hardware shift for mobile photography [2].

## Is it worth upgrading from an iPhone 14?
Whether the upgrade is worth it depends on whether you prioritize cutting-edge photography or general usability.

**The case for upgrading**
If you want a massive leap in camera capabilities, the jump is substantial. The **iPhone 18 Pro** series introduces manual-style control over depth of field via variable aperture, a feature not present on the iPhone 14 [2]. You would also gain access to the latest features like the **iPhone Duo**'s specific ecosystem or the improvements seen in the **iPhone 17** series, such as better Ultra Wide sensors and ProMotion/Always-On displays which were previously Pro-only [2].

**The case against upgrading**
The iPhone 14 remains a "reliable, well-rounded" device in 2026 [3]. It offers a strong price-to-performance ratio for those who don't need flagship-level hardware to complete daily tasks [3]. Unless you are specifically looking for the variable aperture lens or the unique form factor of the Duo, the iPhone 14's performance remains capable for standard use [3].
